V
Classic literature achieves enduring power by
using tightly woven narrative structures to
amplify universal human truths. Through
deliberate choices in architecture—such as
parallel subplots, framed narratives, or cyclical
character arcs—authors transform abstract
concepts like morality, isolation, and ambition
into felt emotional realities.
Theme and structure operate as interdependent
systems in classic novels. Structural frameworks
do not merely contain the narrative; they directly
generate meaning:
Framed & Epistolary Structures: Used in
novels like Frankenstein and Wuthering
Heights to build distance, layer
perspectives, and explore the subjectivity
of truth and memory.
